What I didn't expect is that the new grill doesn't get as hot as the old one, which still cooked just fine but had rusted out at the bottom of its structure. I'm cooking at nearly the hottest setting, but even if I move it to hottest, it still won't cook as fast or brown meat as well as the old grill. Disappointed, to say the least. This said, I think Weber is still a better grill than the other brands on the market and hope the prices don't keep rising because they're about to get up to an unaffordable level.

Results.ReviewText: The new E325 replaced my old E320 after 11 years of service. Given we live near the Atlantic ocean, the old unit held up pretty well. The shell was nearly intact (slight rust) but the flavor bars had to be replaced several times, and finally the gas manifolds and connecting tubes all fell apart. Both are 3 burner models. The new one was less money than to old one (no side burner that never got used), but the construction is a lot flimsier - thin walls, door, cheap wheels and axles, only 2 wheels not 4, no wheel locks, grill is a casting not SS rods. So given inflation, the new unit was far less expensive than the original. The E325 has high-temp setting on the center & right burners for searing (old one didn't), and it seems to preheat faster. Cooking is about the same, and produces excellent cooked foods. The side tables fold down, a nice feature. I bought a pressure gauge to check the propane level; it works but is very hard to read since the tank is under the grill. It takes a small mirror to see the gauge dial. The burners blew out once because of a breeze. Perhaps I will need to block off one side of the grill's air-holes because I grill year-round. The ACE people were excellent in delivery and placing it on our deck.
Results.Title: E325 replaced E320

Results.ReviewText:
Grilling with the E-325 propane grill is quick, easy, and convenient. Charcoal grills have their place, but in our case, since we have a covered lanai and have to move the charcoal grill from the lanai to the yard whenever we use it (so we don't smoke ourselves out), we decided to add a propane grill to our cooking arsenal.

The E-325 fits our needs perfectly. It's a good size both for transport in the back of our car from the local Lowe's warehouse and for daily use on the lanai.

The three burners get the grill up to temperature quickly and it's very easy to maintain a precise temperature with the control knobs. Usability is great. While casters on the two feet that don't have wheels would have made the grill easier to move around, the overall design is still user-friendly. The one-handed burner lighting and the integrated work surfaces - with their hammered steel look and built-in tool hangers - are pretty nice features. The burners seem well-protected so maintenance should be easy.  We've used this just a few times now, and each time the grill has worked great without any problems or issues.

Aesthetically, I really prefer the black enamel look for where we have this grill located. It's low-key and utilitarian versus shiny and excessive. We've always had stainless steel grills at our primary residence, and while stainless can look good (especially when new) it's sort of a pain to keep it looking good. A cleaning product like "Bar Keepers Friend"  is essential for stainless steel maintenance. All you'll need is a soapy wet sponge for cleaning the exterior of the Weber E-325.

This grill has been enjoyable to use and has produced good results. We can't ask for much more.
Results.Title: Nice Grill

Results.ReviewText:
When paying a premium price for a grill, I expected a much better build quality than what is apparent with my E325. The small plastic wheels don’t roll easily (especially on rough surfaces or grass), and the axle they are mounted on noticeably bends and flexes under the weight they’re trying to support. I expected this unit to be much easier to roll around than my previous (cheaper) grill, but alas, it is more difficult. The grill itself works well enough, but it’s hard to tell if the burner has been lit when you initially start it. You can’t see the flame. I put my hand over it to feel the heat if/when it lights. 
I do like how the heat is well distributed, fairly even across the whole grill surface. 
I wish there was some kind of screen across the back to keep mice and squirrels out, or an enclosure on the back of the control box. The wires on my last grill were chewed up by squirrels; I’m afraid of that happening again with my new, much more expensive grill.
Results.Title: The cooking is good, but…

Results.ReviewText: This is not the first Weber grill I’ve owned.  I just replaced my last one that I bought in 2002 and was still working although it was starting to show its age.  But that’s why I bought another one, they’re built to last.
Results.Title: Longevity.

Results.ReviewText:
This is my 2nd Spirit grill. After years of replacing parts on my first I decided it was time for a new one. The 3rd burner in the same sized grill and sear functions are great changes. The grill works great!
For some reason Weber replace the 4 swiveling caster wheel with 2 fixed wheels. For anyone who needs to maneuver the grill in a small space (balcony, patio, etc) this is a problem. 
I communicated with Weber customer service several times asking about a way to attach casters. The only response was no and anything I might do would invalidate the warranty. NOT helpful. 
I ended up removing the wheels and legs and placing the grill on a small furniture moving dolly. 
😁
Results.Title: Grills well, functions iffy

Results.ReviewText:
I love my new Weber grill! After experiencing other brands (ex-spouse didn’t know that the extra money spent provides durability and better results), I knew what I wanted and I had no trouble with spending more for this grill! 
Cooking for one, I only needed a small grill so I got a 3 burner. I had natural gas and made use of that to avoid getting propane tanks. 
I find lighting the grill to have a learning curve. Trying to see the flame is nearly impossible so you really need to feel for the heat or try to sniff to see if you smell gas to know you have a flame. 
The searing ability is nice. You do need to wait until you get a hot grill first. It isn’t instantly able to sear when it’s first lit. 
I’m thrilled with my purchase of a Weber Spirit E325NG. I would recommend this brand to anyone and this sized grill for smaller households.
Results.Title: Love my Spirit E325NG grill!!

Results.ReviewText: So happy with new grill. Easy to light and clean. It cooks evenly too. My last Weber grill lasted for 20 years. I knew I wanted another Weber.

Results.ReviewText: Wanted to make the switch from propane to natural gas and, after shopping several makes and models of grills, the E-325 is a standout.  Excellent cooking surface with plenty of room for the two of us, but also works when the family comes over.  Love the new ignition system which is a big improvement over my previous Weber grills.  Easy to clean drip pan, movability, and drop down side shelves are great features.  Finding that this grill has even heat distribution with easy heat adjustment.
